text.p: General Motors Corp. said Monday it is recalling the first 1,400 all-new 1997 Corvettes it has produced because of potential rear suspension problems that could pose a safety threat.

GM spokesman Kyle Johnson said 500 of vehicles have been delivered to customers. The company has not received any reports of accidents or injuries from the problem, which was discovered by GM employees driving the cars.
Because of a supplier problem, the car's rear suspension tie rod, which controls the angle of the rear wheel and tire, was not properly heat-treated, Johnson said.
Johnson declined to identify the supplier.

GM began calling the 500 customer who have the cars last Friday. It will take dealers an estimated two to three hours to replace the parts, he said. Vehicles now being produced at GM's Corvette plant in Bowling Green, Ky., have been checked for the problem, Johnson said.
The recall mars a much-hyped introduction GM has been conducting for the sports car, which was unveiled Jan. 6 and officially went on sale March 7.

GM is spending an estimated $25 million on the Corvette advertising campaign, according to the trade magazine Advertising Age. GM was scheduled to air its television ad for the Corvette during Hollywood's Academy Awards Monday night.
Johnson said GM was not worried the recall will dampen enthusiasm for the product.
"We're really not concerned about that. It's an outstanding design," he said.

The 1997 Corvette is the fifth generation of the famed Detroit muscle car and the first major redesign since 1984. The car features a new, lightweight engine, a stiffer frame, new suspension, as well as more interior and cargo room.
GM's stock edged up 37.5 cents to $57.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
